name: Serve Activation
focus: Shoulder and rotational activation for serve
description: Shoulder and core activation complex specifically designed to prepare the serving motion. Focuses on rotator cuff activation, scapular stability, and rotational mobility.
coachingNotes: Focus on shoulder blade control. Move slowly and with control. Avoid shrugging shoulders. Maintain neutral spine throughout all movements.

name: Lateral Movement Prep
description: Lateral movement and footwork activation complex. Prepares the hips, knees, and ankles for the side-to-side demands of tennis. Focuses on proper landing mechanics and quick direction changes.
coachingNotes: Focus on soft landings with knees tracking over toes. Maintain athletic stance throughout. Control the lateral movement - don't let the knee cave in.

name: Vertical Power Prep
description: Explosive movement preparation for forward and vertical movements in tennis. Activates the posterior chain and prepares the body for explosive serves, overheads, and forward lunges.
coachingNotes: Land softly with knees slightly bent. Focus on quick ground contact times. Maintain upright torso position. Progress from bodyweight to weighted variations.

name: Shoulder & Elbow Prep
focus: Rotator cuff and elbow injury prevention
description: Injury prevention-focused warm-up targeting common tennis overuse injuries. Includes rotator cuff activation, elbow tendons, and wrist mobility work.
coachingNotes: Move slowly and with control. Focus on areas of tightness or previous injury. Stop if you feel pain (not to be confused with discomfort).

name: Serve Power Chain
description: Rotational power complex designed to improve serve velocity through transverse plane movements. Focuses on explosive hip rotation, shoulder mobility, and core stability specific to the tennis serve motion.
coachingNotes: Focus on explosive rotation. Maintain shoulder stability throughout. Quality over quantity - each rep should mimic serve mechanics. Progress weight gradually while maintaining perfect form.

name: Forehand Stroke Power
description: Rotational power complex for generating maximum forehand power. Focuses on hip-to-shoulder separation, core rotation, and deceleration strength for the follow-through.
coachingNotes: Focus on sequential rotation: hips first, then torso, then shoulders. Generate power from the ground up. Control the eccentric (catch) phase of each throw.

name: Net Play Power
description: Forward power development for explosive net play. Focuses on quick forward movements, overhead strength, and reactive power needed for effective volleying.
coachingNotes: Focus on maximum height and explosive takeoff. Land softly and immediately reset for the next rep. Maintain overhead stability throughout.

name: Return Power
focus: Lateral power for return of serve
description: Lateral power development for explosive return of serve. Focuses on quick lateral movements, explosive pushes off the ground, and generating power from a low position.
coachingNotes: Focus on quick, explosive lateral movements. Stick each landing for 2-3 seconds. Maintain low center of gravity. Drive through the heel of the front foot.

name: Overhead Strength
description: Comprehensive overhead power circuit targeting serve, smash, and overhead clear. Combines rotational power, vertical jump, and overhead stability for complete overhead game development.
coachingNotes: Perform as a circuit with minimal rest between exercises. Focus on explosive, powerful movements. Maintain perfect form even as fatigue sets in.

name: Shoulder Stability
description: Shoulder stability complex for injury prevention and performance. Focuses on rotator cuff endurance, scapular control, and maintaining shoulder health through high-repetition stability work.
coachingNotes: Move slowly and with perfect control. Focus on shoulder blade movement and position. Stop if you feel any shoulder pain. These are prevention exercises - consistency is key.

name: Rotational Core
description: Core stability complex focusing on resisting and controlling rotation. Critical for maintaining posture during powerful tennis strokes and preventing energy leaks in the kinetic chain.
coachingNotes: Focus on maintaining perfect posture - don't let the weight pull you off center. Brace the core as if preparing for a big serve. Control the eccentric (return) phase of each movement.

name: Single-Leg Control
description: Single-leg stability complex for improved balance and control during lateral court movements. Focuses on hip stability, ankle strength, and maintaining posture on one leg.
coachingNotes: Focus on slow, controlled movements. Maintain upright torso position. Land softly with knee tracking over toes. If balance is an issue, use support or reduce range of motion.

name: Lower Body Stability
focus: Lower body joint stability for injury prevention
description: Hip and knee stability complex for preventing common tennis lower body injuries. Focuses on controlling knee valgus, hip stability, and maintaining proper alignment during dynamic movements.
coachingNotes: Focus on maintaining knee alignment with toes. Control the descent phase. Keep weight in the heels. Stop if you feel knee pain (not to be confused with muscle fatigue).

name: Full Body Stability
description: Dynamic stability circuit targeting stability in all planes of motion. Combines upper body, core, and lower body stability exercises to create a comprehensive stability foundation for tennis.
coachingNotes: Perform as a circuit with minimal rest. Focus on maintaining perfect form even as fatigue increases. Breathe steadily throughout.

name: Lateral Quickness
description: Lateral agility complex for improving side-to-side court coverage. Focuses on quick feet, efficient lateral movement, and maintaining balance during rapid direction changes.
coachingNotes: Focus on quick, light feet. Stay low and athletic. Push off the ground explosively. Maintain proper alignment - don't let the knee cave in during lateral movements.

name: Court Movement
description: Forward and backward agility complex for improving court positioning. Focuses on explosive starts, quick stops, and maintaining balance during forward and backward movements.
coachingNotes: Focus on explosive starts and quick stops. Maintain low center of gravity. Land softly and immediately prepare for the next movement. Use a partner or coach for timing.

name: All-Direction Agility
description: Multi-directional agility complex for complete court coverage. Combines lateral, forward, backward, and diagonal movements to prepare for any situation on the tennis court.
coachingNotes: Perform as a circuit. Focus on quick reactions and explosive movements. Maintain athletic stance throughout. Partner should change directions randomly for reactive training.

name: Reaction Training
description: Split step and reaction agility complex for improving the first movement in tennis. Focuses on quick reactions, explosive first steps, and maintaining balance during dynamic starts.
coachingNotes: Focus on reacting to partner's movements with a quick split step. Explode out of the split step into the first movement. Partner should use quick, random movements to simulate match situations.

name: Agility Endurance
description: Agility endurance complex for maintaining quickness and coordination late in matches. Focuses on maintaining movement quality and speed as fatigue sets in.
coachingNotes: Focus on maintaining perfect form even as you fatigue. Keep rest periods short to simulate match conditions. Mental toughness is as important as physical - push through the discomfort.

name: Match Conditioning
description: Tennis-specific conditioning complex simulating match demands. Combines short bursts of high-intensity work with active recovery to mimic the stop-and-go nature of tennis.
coachingNotes: Focus on maintaining good running form throughout. The zone 2 run should be at a conversational pace. Tempo runs should be at 80-85% of max effort. Sled pushes should be explosive.

name: Interval Training
description: High-intensity interval conditioning for tennis. Simulates the repeated sprints and recovery periods of a tennis match. Focuses on improving aerobic and anaerobic capacity.
coachingNotes: Go all-out during work periods. Use active recovery during rest periods (walk, light jog). Focus on quick transitions between work and rest. Monitor heart rate to ensure proper intensity.

name: Lateral Endurance
description: Lateral movement conditioning for improved court coverage endurance. Focuses on building the specific endurance needed for side-to-side tennis movements.
coachingNotes: Focus on maintaining proper form during lateral movements. Keep the chest up and hips back. Use controlled landings. The zone 2 run should be at a steady, maintainable pace.

name: Power Endurance
description: Explosive conditioning complex for maintaining power output throughout long matches. Combines explosive movements with endurance training to build power endurance.
coachingNotes: Focus on maximum explosiveness for each jump. Land softly and immediately prepare for the next rep. Maintain perfect form even as fatigue increases. Sled pushes should be heavy and explosive.

name: Active Recovery
description: Active recovery conditioning complex for days between matches or intense training sessions. Focuses on maintaining fitness while promoting recovery through low-intensity, mobility-focused movements.
coachingNotes: Keep intensity low - this should feel easy. Focus on breathing and relaxation. Use the stretches to work on areas of tightness. Stay hydrated throughout.

name: Post-Match Recovery
description: Immediate post-match recovery complex for reducing soreness and promoting recovery. Should be performed within 30-60 minutes after match completion. Focuses on light mobility work and active recovery.
coachingNotes: Move slowly and gently. Focus on breathing deeply. Don't push through pain - if something hurts, skip it. Hydrate well and consider adding electrolytes.

name: Shoulder Recovery
description: Shoulder-specific recovery complex for maintaining shoulder health after heavy serving or overhead work. Focuses on mobility, blood flow, and gentle activation of the rotator cuff muscles.
coachingNotes: Move very gently and slowly. Focus on relaxation and breathing. If you feel any shoulder pain (not just discomfort), stop immediately. Ice after if shoulders feel inflamed.

name: Leg Recovery
description: Lower body recovery complex for reducing leg soreness and promoting recovery after intense court work. Focuses on hip mobility, leg blood flow, and gentle activation.
coachingNotes: Focus on areas that feel particularly tight or sore. Use the foam roller to work out knots. Keep the run at a very easy pace - you should be able to carry on a conversation.

name: Full Body Recovery
focus: Complete recovery for all muscle groups
description: Full body recovery circuit for comprehensive recovery after intense training or matches. Combines mobility work, light activation, and active recovery for all major muscle groups used in tennis.
coachingNotes: Perform as a circuit with minimal rest. Focus on relaxation and breathing. Move slowly and with control. This should feel easy and refreshing, not challenging.

name: Mobility Recovery
description: Deep mobility and flexibility complex for maintaining and improving range of motion in all joints. Focuses on static stretching, deep mobility work, and relaxation techniques.
coachingNotes: Hold each stretch for the full duration. Focus on deep breathing and relaxation. Don't bounce or force the stretch. Use foam roller on any particularly tight areas.
